newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron says 1996 net at record levels. [CORRECTED 09:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Petron says 1996 net at record levels. [CORRECTED 09:15 GMT]

text.p: Philippine oil refiner Petron Corp said on Thursday that net income in 1996 rose to a record 4.238 (Corrects from 4.328) billion pesos from 4.020 billion pesos in 1995 because of a strong growth in sales.

"Petron's favourable performance was primarily due to larger sales volume, improved operating efficiency and higher non-operating income, which offset the under-recoveries in crude costs," the company said in a statement.

The countries three main oil refiners, which include Petron, are owed some 2.5 billion pesos from the government's Oil Price Stabilisation Fund, set up to protect importers of crude oil from fluctuations in global prices.
The other two large oil refiners in the country are Caltex (Philippines) Inc and Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp.
Petron said sales volumes in 1996 grew 8.1 percent to 58.7 million barrels with sales revenues growing to 53.4 billion pesos from 44.641 billion pesos in 1995.
It said it had a market share of 41.4 percent in the year.

The company said capacity utilisation rose to 93 percent from 90 percent in 1995. It also said that refining capacity would be increased to 180,000 barrels per day from 165,000 bpd in 1995 on the conclusion of an ongoing de-bottlenecking programme.
Assets at the end of 1996 totalled 47.9 billion pesos from 29.5 billion in 1995, the company said. Retained earnings in 1996 were at 9.3 billion pesos, it said.
